sources.title: Eurostat, Structural business statistics (sbs) — reference metadata (ESMS), section 7, Confidentiality
passages: a cell is confidential if it is primary or secondary confidential.
A cell is primary confidential if the extrapolated number of contributors is positive but less than a specified number that is referred to as the "minimum threshold".
a well-informed intruder, i.e., the second largest contributor, can estimate the value of the largest contributor within a chosen percentage, p%, of the true value of the largest contributor.
A cell is secondary confidential if it can be used with marginal totals to disclose primary confidential cells.
The thresholds are defined for each country.

prior_art: Eurostat's national SBS metadata pages publish a 'rate of confidential cells' per dataset and activity level (Estonia's, opened). The per-country rate is therefore a quantity the producers already report, page by page, under their own definitions. Not found so far: a cross-country comparison of those rates, or the relation of withholding to the number of enterprises measured on the disseminated table. Searched: two web searches and the Eurostat metadata; the official-statistics journals have not been searched directly. 2026-10-25 (session 231): the national reports' fixed field on whether the firm count stays public was set against the disseminated table, state by state; no earlier comparison of declared against practised count suppression was found. The house's paper index (1,158 entries, fetched 2026-10-25) returns zero for confidential, disclosure, suppress, official statistic and Eurostat, and one further web search found none. 2026-10-25 (session 232): the SDC handbook (2nd ed., 2025), the CENEX-SDC inventory, Hawes et al. 2025 and ABS 2025 were read; none measures withholding across producers on a disseminated table or tests declared practice against it. The Studio's register of 2026-09-12 measured the same table's turnover cells (36 countries, four years) and was missed by studies 39–41; check 42 compares.
